rows.title: Legacy preset additional-parameter save, apply, and reset
observables: The selected preset snapshots the outgoing global additionalParams value before switching.
The incoming preset applies its additionalParams value without aliasing the stored preset array.
Missing, null, empty, legacy, and non-default values remain distinguishable until the owning normalization rule applies.
The selected value survives SQLite persistence and bootstrap reload.
variants: saveCurrent false and apply false pointer-only selection
normalization: JSON object-key order is ignored.
Array order, missing, null, empty array, and default are semantic and must not be normalized together.

tests: server/fastify/__tests__/commands.test.ts (legacy preset additionalParams save/apply/reset, persistence, and bootstrap matrix)

verification.residual: The baseline omitted this field, so this is verified as an additive Fastify-only preservation rule rather than fork-point parity.

rows.notes: This pilot traces a recent field-completeness omission rather than claiming that the baseline itself preserved preset-scoped additional parameters.

rows.title: Translation preset and model-profile runtime dispatch
observables: Translation uses the selected global or chat-bound translator preset.
An LLM step resolves the selected model profile, model ID, endpoint, runtime options, and additional parameters.
Missing or invalid profile bindings follow the documented legacy/default path rather than a stale profile.
Provider failure returns the translation failure contract without caching a false success.
Preset and profile selection survive reload.
variants: profile with non-default sampler and endpoint options
normalization: Credential bytes are redacted while credential selection and presence remain semantic.
Endpoint path/query, model ID, option values, step order, missing, null, and default are semantic.

verification.residual: The profile abstraction is post-baseline; live third-party transport remains deterministically stubbed while selection, request shape, failure, and reload are production-path tested.

rows.notes: The comparison preserves the baseline's selected translation intent while allowing the Fastify profile representation to differ physically.

rows.title: OpenAI Responses endpoint and request-shape preservation
observables: An explicit model endpoint overrides the generic custom URL.
An already complete Responses path and query string are preserved exactly.
Autofill appends /responses or /v1/responses without moving query parameters.
Request body, resolved model/options, streaming mode, and retry/fallback selection remain owned by the same resolved profile.
normalization: Authorization values are redacted while header presence and credential selection remain semantic.
URL path/query, array order, body values, missing, null, and defaults are semantic; JSON object-key order alone is ignored.

verification.residual: Live third-party retry behavior is fixture-proven rather than exercised against a paid endpoint.

rows.notes: The explicit endpoint rule is byte-for-byte semantic; normalizers may not erase path or query differences.

rows.title: Portable reroll-candidate ordering and identity
observables: Every retained candidate is exported in newest-to-oldest navigation order.
Candidate role, text, message identity, generation metadata, and references survive supported round trips.
Portable import extracts candidates into durable alternate rows without duplicating them into the active transcript.
Hydration and reload reconstruct the candidate buffer so forward/back navigation restores the same displaced tail.
variants: candidate with generationInfo and reference metadata
Original-style block and local-backup codec round trip
normalization: Generated IDs may be normalized only when occurrence order and every identity/reference relationship remain intact.
Candidate order, role, repeated values, metadata presence, missing, null, and empty arrays are semantic.

tests: server/fastify/__tests__/risuSaveCodec.test.ts (export, decode, fresh import, and reload through all supported codecs)

verification.residual: All current raw, compressed, stream, and block .risu codecs pass an exported-byte round trip. Direct execution inside Original RisuAI is infeasible because the pinned harness exposes no save-exchange or durable-reroll seam; reopen when such a seam exists.

rows.notes: Original retained candidates only in a process-local buffer; the Fastify-only persistence must remain additive and must not make shared saves unreadable.

rows.title: Pinned compatibility-baseline materialization and integrity
observables: A clean environment can materialize the exact compatibility-baseline commit in a detached worktree without moving the upstream checkout.
Preflight rejects an absent object, wrong commit, attached branch, dirty worktree, or missing dependency installation.
normalization: The moving upstream checkout, an attached branch, a dirty tree, or a merely similar revision cannot substitute for the exact detached baseline.
rows.notes: The package script owns prepare mode; direct CLI --check owns read-only integrity verification.

rows.title: Shared compatibility case matrix and artifact schema
observables: Baseline and current runners execute the same ordered 16-cell scenario, transport, and say-nothing matrix.
Both sides emit the same closed artifact shape and reject missing, extra, duplicated, or reordered cells.
variants: missing, duplicate, extra, and reordered artifact cells
normalization: Artifact validation is closed-world: case identity, count, order, side, baseline commit, and semantic payload are comparison inputs.
rows.notes: The type contract and runtime validator jointly own the comparable artifact boundary.

rows.title: Semantic compatibility normalizer
observables: Only deterministic fixture IDs, approved volatile generation fields, header casing, and JSON object-key order normalize.
Missing versus null, array order, endpoint identity, message role, and generation metadata presence remain semantic.
normalization: JSON object keys and HTTP header names are canonicalized without sorting semantic arrays or rewriting endpoint URLs.
Absent properties stay absent; explicit null stays null; message roles and metadata presence are preserved.
rows.notes: The c33dac568 production correction proves inactive persisted metadata is fixed at its owner instead of being hidden by normalization; 5b6a9d492 preserves the distinct prompt-preview diagnostic contract.

rows.title: Fixture, golden, and expected-difference governance
observables: Fixture source digests, the exact 16 case IDs, deterministic inputs, and the exact golden artifact set are fail-closed.
Every observed divergence must match one decision-backed inventory mapping and its semantic digest; golden updates require an explicit review reason.
variants: unregistered, stale, duplicated, or unsigned expected difference
normalization: A changed semantic digest is a new difference and cannot inherit approval from a stale mapping.
Generated actual artifacts never become authority unless the explicit reviewed update command refreshes the governed goldens and manifests.
rows.notes: The governed register currently owns 23 cell/aspect mappings across 15 divergent cells; no anonymous exception is accepted. Fixture provenance classifies every source at 546ea5aae, after 5b6a9d492 separated prompt-preview diagnostics from persisted transcript metadata.

rows.title: Compatibility register authority and fail-closed validation
observables: Inventory, finding, decision, and upstream-unit documents satisfy their JSON schemas and cross-register references.
Duplicate stable IDs or raw source IDs, malformed commits, inconsistent decisions or dispositions, and incomplete or reordered upstream coverage fail validation.
variants: duplicate stable or raw source ID
malformed or reordered upstream commit coverage
normalization: Register validation preserves missing, null, array order, repeated values, and endpoint identity as distinct semantic inputs.
rows.notes: Register and schema changes are also routed to this validator by affected-test selection.

rows.title: Affected compatibility test selection
observables: Harness and baseline infrastructure changes select focused validation plus the full pinned differential.
Register authority changes select fail-closed register validation and tests, while compatibility-relevant production changes select the current-only compatibility lane.
variants: browser, protocol, or Fastify production change
normalization: Path selection is additive and deduplicated; a focused test does not replace required current-only or full pinned compatibility proof.
rows.notes: Selection tests cover compatibility infrastructure, register authority, production paths, and workflow parity.

rows.title: Aggregate compatibility quality-lane ownership
observables: The regular aggregate includes fail-closed register validation and a current-only compatibility lane.
Current-only compatibility runs after register validation and remains isolated from concurrently mutating lanes.
normalization: Aggregate success requires both compatibility lanes; dependency or isolation metadata cannot silently drop either lane.
rows.notes: The external pinned differential remains intentionally outside the ordinary aggregate because it owns a separately prepared worktree.

rows.title: CI cadence, artifact, and release-equivalent compatibility ownership
observables: Main quality CI requires register validation before current-only compatibility and retains current artifacts for triage.
The full pinned differential runs on a daily schedule and manual dispatch, prepares the exact baseline, and retains its evidence.
Release-equivalent evidence combines successful main quality lanes with a successful full pinned differential for the exact candidate revision.
normalization: A current-only success cannot be reported as pinned parity, and a scheduled result from another revision cannot satisfy release-equivalent evidence.
rows.notes: Quality CI owns always-on register/current proof; the separate workflow owns the environment-heavy pinned proof and 14-day evidence retention.

rows.title: Recovery lineage through command responses and server-sent events

rows.title: Writer, observer, outbox, receipt, and replay recovery lifecycle
observables: Only the active writer mutates; observers consume ordered invalidations and can promote only through the explicit takeover lifecycle.
